messages:
anya: FYI — we got a high-severity from support: multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on rdx-chat-3-b after last night's runtime deploy :rotating_light:
eli: seeing the alert in datadog too, p95 up ~30% and p99 up ~70% for token-generation requests since 02:00 UTC
michael: any obvious correlation with model/seq-length? which kernel got picked in the rollout?
anya: support attached a repro curl that hits a long-chat session (avg seq ~1024) — sending it to the thread: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rdx-chat-3-b","input":"...long convo..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
eli: quick look at logs: kernel-selection heuristic flipped to prefer SDPA variant for seq >512 in the new compileflags patch (candidate-compileflag v2). On paper it's faster, but p99 is worse here — looks like memory churn + fallback thrash under mixed batch sizes.
support-jordan: customers are on Dedicated and Hosted; one reported timeout at 1.5s (their SLO is 1s) — they're pretty upset.
kenneth: can we toggle the heuristic back? is there a runtime flag/override?
anya: yes — runtime supports per-model kernel overrides. I can force FlashAttention for rdx-chat-3-b while we investigate. Command:

```
redwoodctl runtime kernel-override set --model rdx-chat-3-b --kernel flashattn --reason "p99 regression rollback"
```

eli: do it please and note the change in incident channel. That should be safe and immediate.
anya: done — override applied, routing shows kernels switching now. SRE Bot: `sre-bot: kernel-override applied by anya for rdx-chat-3-b -> flashattn (scoped)`
michael: metrics already improving for the affected hosts, p99 trending down. Thanks.
support-jordan: relaying to customers now — ETA for full mitigation?
eli: mitigation standing by as long-term fix, we'll revert the compile flag or tweak heuristic. Next steps: reproduce locally, capture flamegraphs, and run the repro harness across batch-size mix to confirm thrash pattern.
mania (typo, ignore): :eyes:
kenneth: request: capture `KVCache` memstats and kernel selection traces for the burst window. Add tag `incident/3176543210` so we can slice traces.
anya: started a repro run in the perf cluster with the exact customer payload and interleaved small/large batches. Repro command:

```
perf-harness run --model rdx-chat-3-b --workload-file customer_long_mixed.json --collect flame,kv,trace --tag incident-3176543210
```

eli: raw results: SDPA path shows 1.9x higher tail compared to flashattn for mixed batches; CPU pinned on the host during fallback; memory allocs spike. Looks like SDPA kernel uses a different workspace allocator that conflicts with our continuous-batching pool and triggers fragmentation.
michael: ok that explains p99. We need two things: 1) rollback candidate compileflag v2 on the next hotfix, 2) add a kernel-selection safety gate so SDPA is only chosen when batch-size distribution is narrow and seq lengths > threshold.
anya: I've opened a PR for a heuristic change: require both avg_seq > 800 AND 95th_seq > 900 AND batch_variance < 0.15 to pick SDPA. PR link: https://git.redwood/infruntime/heuristics/pull/412 (note: draft).
eli: also add a temporary conservative compileflag that disables SDPA for multi-tenant hosted pools until we ship the heuristic. We can keep SDPA enabled for dedicated clusters with uniform workloads.
deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: rolled back compileflags/candidate-compileflag:v2 -> v1 on cluster-perf-1 (manual)`
anya: rolling the compileflag rollback to canary in production for hosted pools now; will monitor p99 for the next 20m.
kenneth: please also add telemetry counters: kernel_selected={flashattn,sdpa,sdpa_fallback} and fallback_reason tags. We need to see where fallback happens and why.
eli: added telemetry patch in staging, will ship with the rollback so we get postmortem data.
support-jordan: customers notified and most are seeing improvement after override. One dedicated customer still has spikes — they're pinned to a hardware family that uses different kernel binaries, checking with infra.
michael: infra note: some older CUDA runtimes had a bug in cuMemAllocAsync that made SDPA worse; confirm their nodes are on cuda 12.2 vs 12.6 we test on.
anya: summary for incident ticket: immediate: per-model kernel override (flashattn) applied; canary rollback of compileflag v2 initiated; mid-term: refine selection heuristic + telemetry; long-term: make workspace allocator robust to continuous-batching memory patterns.
eli: leaving a follow-up task to run a full canary for 6 hours and then schedule a change-control for heuristic patch. I'll own the postmortem.
kenneth: assign action items and ETA in the ticket, include customer impact table.
anya: created incident ticket INC-2026-3176543210 with timeline and mitigation steps, linking support threads.
support-jordan: customers acknowledged — closing customer-facing loop, will escalate if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
eli: thanks team. Postmortem checklist: logs, perf artifacts, deploy diff, telemetry graphs, and a risk matrix for enabling SDPA by model/hardware.
anya: will share a writeup in eng-runtime after we collect traces.
anya: closing thread here, will reopen if p99 climbs again.
